name: Custom Excel / Google Sheets Tool Built for You in 48 Hours — Tracker, Calculator, Dashboard or Data Clean-up
summary: Download the intake pack, fill in the nine-question brief, get a working spreadsheet built to it within 48 hours. One revision included.
description_html:
A custom Excel or Google Sheets tool built to your brief in 48 hours — tracker, calculator, dashboard or data clean-up, with the formulas checked and a how-to page.

You know what you need to track. You just don't want to lose a weekend fighting formulas.

You download the Project Brief & Intake Pack the moment you buy. It is a short workbook: a nine-question brief, a tab to paste a sample of your data into, and a one-page explanation of how the build runs. Fill it in — about five minutes — and send it back. Your spreadsheet is built from it and delivered within 48 hours.

What you get back

  • A working spreadsheet built to your brief — not a template with your name on it
  • Formulas checked, dropdowns where a list belongs, a dashboard that updates itself
  • A one-page how-to written for your sheet
  • Opens in Excel (2016+) and Google Sheets. No macros, nothing to install
  • One revision round to get it right

Good fits

  • Client, invoice and payment trackers
  • Pricing, quote and margin calculators
  • Inventory and cost-of-goods tracking
  • A KPI dashboard built from a CSV export
  • Turning a messy sheet into one that actually calculates

The 48 hours starts when your completed brief arrives, not at checkout, so there is no clock running while you think about it.

Want to see the standard of work first? Fair — this is a custom build and you cannot preview it. So download something I have already made: the free reseller profit-after-fees calculator. It is free, needs no email, and every rate in it carries the date it was last checked. If that is the standard you want applied to your problem, the brief is the next step.

Not a fit: macros/VBA, live database or API connections, anything that files tax for you, or ongoing data entry. If your brief turns out to need one of those you will be told straight away and refunded, rather than handed something half-built.
